links.outcome: Model accuracy on external-institution radiographs versus manual ground truth
links.effect: No significant differences between predicted and ground truth: SVA 50.7 vs 52.3 mm (p=0.85); PT 27.6 vs 30.5° (p=0.24); PI 58.0 vs 61.8° (p=0.17); LL 40.4 vs 42.4° (p=0.77); T1PA 24.8 vs 28.0° (p=0.21).
links.quote: SpinePose accurately predicted all 5 spinopelvic parameters without any statistically significant differences: SVA, 50.7 mm vs 52.3 mm (p = 0.85); PT, 27.6° vs 30.5° (p = 0.24); PI, 58.0° vs 61.8° (p = 0.17); LL, 40.4° vs 42.4° (p = 0.77); and T1PA, 24.8° vs 28.0° (p = 0.21) when comparing ground truth annotations with predicted values.

screen.reason: This is an external validation study testing the generalizability of an imaging AI model (SpinePose) on a retrospective cohort from another institution. It does not evaluate a clinical deployment practice or safeguard.
